newsitem.title: USA: Detroit newspaper workers to hold press conference.
newsitem.headline: Detroit newspaper workers to hold press conference.

text.p: The Metropolitan Council of Newspaper Unions scheduled a news conference for late Friday afternoon amid numerous reports the unions were going to make an unconditional offer to return to work at Detroit's two major daily papers.

About 2,500 workers went on strike in July 1995 after they failed to come to contract terms with the Detroit Free Press and Detroit News. The Free Press is owned by Knight-Ridder Inc, while Gannett Co Inc owns the News.

A representative from the unions could not be immediately reached for comment. On Thursday, union spokeswoman Nancy Dunn said an offer to return to work has been discussed for months and continues to be an option.
Both the Free Press and News reported Friday the unions were close to ending their walkout.
